title: Greenland or Else: Trump Threatens NATO Ally with Military Force Over Arctic Island
synopsis: Beginning in January 2025 and continuing through mid-2025, Trump repeatedly refused to rule out military force to annex Greenland from Denmark, a fellow NATO member. On March 29, 2025, Trump told NBC News I never take military force off the table regarding Greenland. Vice President JD Vance visited the island in March 2025, accusing Denmark of doing a bad job protecting it. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen traveled to Greenland in April 2025 and warned: You can't annex other countries, calling US pressure unacceptable. Polls showed the vast majority of Greenlanders oppose joining the US. The threats shattered norms of territorial sovereignty among Western allies and alarmed European governments at a moment of heightened tensions with Russia.

title: Take Back the Canal: Trump Vows to Seize Panama Canal on Inauguration Day
synopsis: During his January 20, 2025 inauguration speech, Trump vowed the United States would take back the Panama Canal, falsely claiming China was operating it. Panama's Foreign Minister Javier Martinez-Acha responded that the only hands operating the canal are Panamanian. Panama formally alerted the UN Security Council on January 21, 2025, citing the UN Charter's prohibition on threats of force against territorial integrity. Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino called Trump's claims lies and said Canal sovereignty was non-negotiable and sealed. The crisis forced Secretary of State Rubio to make Panama his first international stop, where he acknowledged no deal on canal control was forthcoming. Trump's false narrative about Chinese soldiers in the Canal sparked a nationalist backlash inside Panama.

title: Canada as the 51st State: Trump's Annexation Campaign Against America's Closest Ally
synopsis: From late 2024 into 2025, Trump relentlessly pushed the idea that Canada should become the 51st state of the United States, pairing the rhetoric with escalating tariff threats. On February 1, 2025, Trump imposed 25% tariffs on Canadian goods. By July 10, 2025, Trump sent a letter to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing an increase to 35%, effective August 1, 2025, threatening further hikes if Canada retaliated. Canadian polls showed support for joining the US dropped to just 4 percent, while nationalist sentiment surged. The AP reported in October 2025 that all thirteen Canadian premiers had made an unprecedented joint trip to Washington to defend their interests. Trump cited fentanyl concerns despite Canada accounting for only a minor fraction of US fentanyl supply.

title: Ukraine Arms Cutoff: Trump Halts Weapons to Kyiv Days After Oval Office Blowup with Zelensky
synopsis: On March 3-4, 2025, the Trump administration paused all future US military aid deliveries to Ukraine, just days after a televised Oval Office confrontation between Trump and President Zelensky on February 28. The New York Times reported the weapons flow had essentially stopped for 50 days prior to the meeting. The White House said the pause would last until Ukraine's leaders showed good-faith commitment to peace. Trump's Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had already declared that Ukraine joining NATO was impractical and regaining occupied territory illusionary. All Biden-era arms shipments in transit were halted, including weapons on aircraft and ships headed to Poland. European allies scrambled to fill the gap as Russia escalated its offensive.

title: Putin's Peace Plan: Trump Pushes Ukraine to Surrender Entire Donbas to Russia
synopsis: In November and December 2025, a draft peace plan obtained by the AP showed Trump's proposal would require Ukraine to cede large swaths of territory to Russia, including the entire Donbas, and limit the size of Kyiv's military — terms described as decidedly favorable to Russia. On October 20, 2025, CNN reported that a Trump-Zelensky working lunch turned acrimonious when Trump insisted on territorial concessions and raised his voice repeatedly. Ukrainian officials told Axios in December 2025 that after Trump envoys Witkoff and Kushner held a five-hour meeting with Putin, the US proposal worsened: It felt like the US was trying to sell us the Russian desire to take the whole of Donbas. Zelensky refused to accept terms he said violated the Ukrainian constitution and international law.

title: 145% Tariffs on China: Trump Launches the Most Destructive Trade War Since the Great Depression
synopsis: On April 2, 2025 — Liberation Day — Trump announced sweeping reciprocal tariffs, then escalated China-specific tariffs to 145% by April 9 after Beijing retaliated with its own duties. The Yale Budget Lab calculated this raised the US average effective tariff rate to 27%, the highest since 1903. Economists projected a $4,700 per-household purchasing power loss in 2025 dollars, and Yale estimated long-run GDP would be 0.6% permanently smaller — equivalent to $170 billion annually. The CBO projected tariffs would reduce US payroll employment by 740,000 by year-end 2025. One toy company CEO called it end of days, estimating his tariff bill would explode from $2.3 million to over $20 million. A temporary US-China truce on May 12, 2025 reduced rates to 30%, but the structural damage to global supply chains persisted.

title: Europe Under Fire: Trump's Liberation Day Tariffs Trigger Transatlantic Trade War
synopsis: On April 2, 2025, Trump imposed 20% reciprocal tariffs on the European Union, on top of 25% tariffs already in place on European steel, aluminum, and cars. The EU approved its first retaliatory measures on April 9, 2025, targeting $23 billion worth of US goods at 25% — from almonds and motorcycles to yachts — aimed at products from Republican-leaning US states. The European Central Bank estimated a 0.3-0.5 percentage point hit to eurozone growth. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen paused EU retaliation for 90 days to match Trump's pause but warned countermeasures would kick in if negotiations failed. Trump called the EU formed in order to screw the United States at a February 2025 cabinet meeting, deepening fears in Brussels that his true goal was dismantling the alliance.

title: WHO Withdrawal: Trump Abandons Global Health Agency on Day One of Second Term
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, hours after taking office, Trump signed an executive order withdrawing the United States from the World Health Organization. The US was the WHO's largest financial contributor. Trump cited mishandling of COVID-19 and what he claimed were disproportionate US financial obligations, ignoring that China has 300% of the US population yet contributes 90% less. The WHO warned the withdrawal could jeopardize emergency health programs globally. Congress had not been consulted — the WHO's own 1948 charter requires one year's notice and fulfillment of current financial obligations. The WHO expressed regret and urged reconsideration. The withdrawal, Trump's second attempt after his 2020 effort was reversed by Biden, removed the US from pandemic preparedness negotiations and International Health Regulations amendments.

title: Paris Agreement Withdrawal 2.0: Trump Exits Climate Accord Again on Inauguration Day
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing the US to immediately withdraw from the Paris Climate Agreement for the second time, having previously exited in 2020 only to have Biden rejoin in 2021. The order also ended US participation in all UN Framework Convention on Climate Change commitments and immediately ceased future financial transfers to climate programs. The UN World Meteorological Organization noted 2024 was the hottest year on record at 1.55 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. The EU's Ursula von der Leyen vowed Europe would stay the course, while the European Parliament held emergency debates on the geopolitical implications. The withdrawal again removed the world's largest historical greenhouse gas emitter from global climate governance at the worst possible moment.

title: Article 5 Doubt: Trump Publicly Questions NATO's Mutual Defense Guarantee Before Hague Summit
synopsis: On June 24, 2025, while flying to the NATO summit in the Netherlands, Trump publicly cast doubt on whether the United States would honor Article 5 — the alliance's core mutual defense commitment — telling reporters there were numerous definitions of the clause. The statement alarmed allies already unsettled by months of US hostility. Though Trump eventually reaffirmed a nominal Article 5 commitment at the summit and secured a new 5% GDP defense spending target, the New York Times reported the summit's language was deliberately mushy, pledging that allies — not all allies — would meet the target. Spain formally opted out. A Reuters summary noted the event was tailor-made to placate Trump. The episode gave Putin a strategic gift, confirming European fears that Washington's security guarantee was transactional and unreliable.

title: Gaza Ethnic Cleansing Plan: Trump Proposes Expelling 2 Million Palestinians to Egypt and Jordan
synopsis: On January 25, 2025, Trump told reporters he wanted to just clean out Gaza and have Egypt and Jordan permanently absorb its more than 2 million Palestinian residents, calling Gaza a mess and offering Palestinians a beautiful new land. On February 4, 2025, standing beside Netanyahu, Trump said Palestinians had no alternative but to leave and that the US would take over the territory to rebuild it as a Riviera of the Middle East. Human Rights Watch called it an alarming escalation of forced displacement and ethnic cleansing. Both Egypt and Jordan flatly refused. Germany, Australia, Ireland, the UK, Brazil, China, and Russia all rejected the plan. Far-right Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich welcomed the proposal and said he was preparing an operational plan to implement it.

title: Rehab for Putin: Trump's February 2025 Call Ends Three Years of Russia Isolation
synopsis: On February 12, 2025, Trump spoke with Vladimir Putin for over an hour, effectively ending the three-year US-led effort to isolate Russia for its invasion of Ukraine. The call covered not just the war but global energy markets, the dollar's role, the Middle East, and artificial intelligence — exactly the broad bilateral agenda Putin had long sought. Before the call, Trump's Defense Secretary had declared Ukrainian NATO membership impractical and the return of occupied territories illusionary. The New York Times reported that rarely was a policy change between Moscow and Washington so swift and drastic. The AP noted Trump was giving his blessing to key items on Putin's wish list before any settlement was reached. European leaders described the moment as handing Moscow the gift that eluded it during the Cold War.

title: $142 Billion Swords for Despots: Trump's Saudi Arabia Arms Mega-Deal Sidelines Human Rights
synopsis: On May 13, 2025, during a Gulf tour focused on securing investment pledges, Trump signed a $142 billion arms deal with Saudi Arabia — described by the White House as the largest defense cooperation agreement in US history. The agreement covered air and missile defense, space advancement, maritime security, and communications across more than a dozen US defense companies. Trump also announced the lifting of all US sanctions on Syria on a request from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the man US intelligence had concluded ordered the 2018 murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi. Reuters noted the trip sealed the emergence of a new Sunni-led Middle East order that left Israel sidelined. The White House claimed over $2 trillion in total Gulf investment commitments, though Reuters' own tally put specific deals at closer to $730 billion.

title: Signal Chat Contempt: Senior US Officials Mock European Allies in Leaked War Planning Thread
synopsis: In March 2025, a Signal group chat among top US security officials — including National Security Adviser Michael Waltz, Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller — was accidentally exposed when Atlantic editor Jeffrey Goldberg was added to the thread. Beyond the classified Houthi strike details, European allies were horrified by the conversation's explicit contempt: Vance complained about European freeloading, Waltz lamented Europe's weak naval forces, and Miller argued that if the US restored freedom of navigation at great cost there needs to be some further gain extracted in return. An EU official told the BBC officials were sick to their stomach. The leak came days after Vance had scandalized European leaders at the Munich Security Conference by calling their political values the enemy within.

title: Kim Snubs Trump: North Korea Fires Missiles, Ignores Every Diplomatic Overture
synopsis: Throughout 2025 and into 2026, Trump repeatedly expressed eagerness to meet Kim Jong Un, calling him an old friend and saying he would love a meeting, but North Korea systematically rebuffed every approach. During Trump's October 2025 Asia trip, Kim launched cruise missiles on October 22 and 28 and sent his foreign minister to Moscow to meet Putin — timed explicitly to coincide with Trump's South Korea visit. Trump admitted the summit never worked out. A North Korean vice foreign minister called US denuclearization demands a pipedream on November 1, 2025. The Stimson Center noted that North Korea's deepened Russia partnership, its codified nuclear doctrine permitting preemptive strikes, and Kim's demand that the US abandon denuclearization as a precondition made any deal structurally impossible. A May 2026 trip to Beijing also produced no Trump-Kim meeting.

title: CECOT Torture Pipeline: Trump Ships 252 Venezuelans to El Salvador Dungeon
synopsis: On March 15-16, 2025, the Trump administration invoked the 1798 Alien Enemies Act to deport 238-252 Venezuelan migrants to El Salvador's Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT) megaprison, paying the Bukele government $6 million for a one-year renewable term. The U.S. government flew deportees with little or no due process, defying a federal court order by Judge James Boasberg. A November 2025 joint report by Human Rights Watch and Cristosal, based on interviews with 40 of the detainees, documented systematic beatings, sexual abuse, solitary confinement as punishment, incommunicado detention, denial of adequate food and medical care, and conditions that drove detainees to the brink of suicide. Investigators found many deportees had no criminal record in the U.S. or abroad, and the groups concluded the U.S. was complicit in torture, enforced disappearances and other violations. The men were eventually returned to Venezuela in a prisoner swap after months of imprisonment.

title: ICE Detention Death Toll Hits Historic High: 52 Dead in 500 Days
synopsis: Between January 20, 2025 and June 4, 2026, 52 people died in ICE immigration detention — the highest mortality rate in over a decade, nearly four times the rate of the Biden administration, and more than double the first Trump term. A June 2026 joint report by Human Rights Watch and Physicians for Human Rights found the mortality rate exceeded even the COVID-19 pandemic peak. The Trump administration expanded the detained population to a record 71,000 by January 2026, a 77 percent increase year-over-year, while deaths tripled. One death at Camp East Montana in El Paso was ruled a homicide by the El Paso County Medical Examiner: Geraldo Lunas Campos died of asphyxia due to neck and torso compression. An AP investigation found at least 10 detainees died by suicide, compared with one in all of 2024. The administration simultaneously dismantled independent DHS oversight mechanisms and delayed the legally required 48-hour public reporting of deaths.

title: Family Separation 2.0: 600 Migrant Children Taken From Parents Nationwide
synopsis: By November 2025, ICE had placed a record 600 immigrant children into federal shelter custody — more than the previous four years combined and the highest number since record-keeping began. Unlike the 2018 zero-tolerance border policy, the new separations occurred inside the country: parents facing deportation were told they could take their child back to a dangerous home country, or their child would be transferred to a federal shelter for unaccompanied minors. In one documented May 2025 case reported by The New York Times, Russian asylum-seeking couple Evgeny and Evgeniia had their 8-year-old son Maksim taken as they were sent to detention in New Jersey. Under Trump, the average shelter stay grew to 217 days — up from one month under Biden. Florida law enforcement arrested at least 47 children on immigration charges. The government also cut legal services for children and issued 72-hour departure ultimatums.

title: Trans Military Purge and Healthcare Ban: Thousands of Troops Discharged
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order reinstating the transgender military ban, declaring that the government recognizes only two immutable biological sexes. The Supreme Court allowed the ban to take effect on May 6, 2025, in a 5-4 ruling. On May 12, 2025, the Pentagon halted all new hormone treatments and surgical procedures for transgender troops via internal memo, beginning the formal process of discharging thousands of service members. A separate January 28, 2025 executive order cut federal funding for gender-affirming care for anyone under 19, directed Medicaid and TRICARE to exclude such treatments, and ordered the DOJ to pursue enforcement against hospitals providing the care. The administration also removed nonbinary gender markers from federal identification documents including passports, forcing transgender Americans to carry documentation inconsistent with their identity.

title: DEI Obliteration: Executive Orders Erase Decades of Civil Rights Infrastructure
synopsis: On January 20-21, 2025, Trump signed two executive orders — EO 14151 Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programs and EO 14152 Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity — requiring all federal agencies to terminate DEI offices, equity action plans, diversity-related grants, and Chief Diversity Officer positions within 60 days. EO 14152 revoked landmark civil rights executive orders dating back to Lyndon Johnson, including the foundational 1965 affirmative action order EO 11246, and directed federal contractors to certify they do not operate DEI programs. OPM Acting Director Charles Ezell ordered all DEIA employees placed on paid administrative leave immediately, with agency heads required to develop reduction-in-force plans. The orders also directed the Attorney General to identify up to nine civil compliance investigations of universities, corporations, and nonprofits engaged in illegal DEI practices.

title: DOJ Declares Disabled People Have No Right to Live Outside Institutions
synopsis: In June 2026, the Department of Justice's Office of Legal Counsel issued a 39-page memo declaring that neither the Americans with Disabilities Act nor Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act require states to provide services allowing people with disabilities to remain in their homes rather than institutions. This reversed the federal government's interpretation of the landmark 1999 Supreme Court Olmstead v. L.C. ruling, which had driven deinstitutionalization for 27 years. The DOJ memo acknowledged its own position is out of step with the common understanding of that decision within the federal courts. Simultaneously, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4, 2025 cut $900 billion-plus from Medicaid over a decade, threatening home care services for millions of disabled Americans. Senator Tammy Duckworth led Senate Democrats in introducing a resolution demanding the opinion be rescinded. Advocates warned the memo would enable states to reverse decades of deinstitutionalization progress without fear of federal enforcement.

title: Voter Suppression by Executive Fiat: Trump Orders Proof-of-Citizenship, Decertifies Voting Machines
synopsis: On March 25, 2025, Trump signed EO 14248 Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections, which the Brennan Center called an illegal attempt to take control of major parts of the nation's election systems. The order unilaterally directed the independent Election Assistance Commission to require passport-level documentation for voter registration — a show-your-papers mandate that, since only about half of Americans hold passports, would disenfranchise millions disproportionately impacting people of color, young voters, and low-income Americans. The order also directed the EAC to decertify all voting machines in 39 states within 180 days and replace them with systems that did not yet exist on the market. It granted Elon Musk's DOGE access to sensitive voter registration files from all 50 states. A federal court permanently blocked the citizenship documentation provision on October 31, 2025, finding the president lacks constitutional authority to alter election procedures.

title: Legal Aid for Migrant Children Gutted: 26,000 Kids Left to Face Courts Alone
synopsis: On February 18-19, 2025, the Trump administration issued a stop-work order via the Interior Department to the Acacia Center for Justice, abruptly halting a $200 million federal contract that provided legal representation to approximately 26,000 unaccompanied migrant children in immigration court. The administration gave no explanation beyond causes outside of your control. The Acacia Center runs the program through a network of 85 organizations nationwide, and the halt left children — some so young their feet could not reach the floor in courtroom chairs — without any attorney. The administration rescinded the first stop-work order but then issued a partial termination on March 21, 2025, cutting funding for legal representation. A federal judge in San Francisco issued a temporary restraining order on April 2, 2025, blocking the cuts. Michael Lukens of the Amica Center called it particularly cruel to make children go to court alone.

title: LGBTQ Asylum Seekers Abandoned: Refugee Cap Slashed 94 Percent, White Afrikaners Prioritized
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump suspended the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program, leaving 128,000 already-vetted refugees — including LGBTQ individuals fleeing persecution — stranded. In October 2025, the White House published a Presidential Determination capping refugee admissions to 7,500 for FY 2026, a 94 percent reduction from Biden's 125,000-person target; most slots were reserved for white South African Afrikaners, descendants of Dutch settlers. A Williams Institute analysis found the cap effectively excluded LGBTQ refugees who disproportionately lack family reunification pathways. The administration also dropped recognition of nonbinary identities on passports and other federal documents, forcing queer asylum seekers to misrepresent themselves on immigration paperwork. Immigration Equality documented a case in which an ICE officer physically restrained an LGBTQ asylum seeker while threatening her wife to self-deport.

title: Sacred Apache Land Fast-Tracked for Foreign Mining Company Over Supreme Court Objection
synopsis: On April 17, 2025, the Trump administration pushed forward the Resolution Copper mine land swap at Oak Flat, Arizona — a sacred Western Apache site called Chi'chil Bildagoteel — ordering the U.S. Forest Service to publish an environmental review by June 16, 2025 to enable the transfer of federal land to Rio Tinto and BHP, two foreign mining companies. The action came while the Supreme Court was still considering whether to hear the Apache Stronghold case challenging the land transfer on religious freedom grounds. A U.S. district court injunction blocked the swap on May 9, 2025. Simultaneously, Trump's DOGE effort directed the closure of more than 25 regional Bureau of Indian Affairs offices nationwide. Eighty-five faith groups and 44 tribal nations supported the Apache appeal, with tribal members describing the destruction of their ancestral ceremonial site as ongoing genocide.

title: Civil Rights Division Hollowed Out: 368 Attorneys Quit as DOJ Targets Reverse Discrimination
synopsis: By July 2025, 368 employees had departed the DOJ Civil Rights Division since Trump's inauguration — an unprecedented exodus representing hundreds of thousands of years of combined experience, according to a congressional memo from Senator Peter Welch. Under Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, the division redirected its mission to investigating alleged reverse discrimination against white Americans, filing a lawsuit against Minnesota's affirmative action hiring policies. In June 2026, the DOJ's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion declaring disparate impact liability — the legal framework used to challenge policies that disproportionately harm minorities — unconstitutional, effectively immunizing policies with racially discriminatory effects. The EEOC dismissed multiple transgender discrimination cases, reversed protections for transgender workers, and its chair Andrea Lucas appealed directly to white men to file discrimination charges.

title: Pentagon Schools Quarantine Books on Race and Gender; DOE Drops Book-Ban Complaints
synopsis: On January 24, 2025, Trump's Education Department dismissed 11 complaints and six allegations related to school book bans filed during the Biden administration, calling them Biden's book ban hoax and eliminating its book ban coordinator position. PEN America had documented over 10,000 book bans in the 2023-2024 school year, nearly triple the prior year. Simultaneously, Pentagon schools serving 67,000 military children worldwide suspended all library access in February 2025 for a compliance review, quarantining books on gender, race, and LGBTQ themes — including To Kill a Mockingbird, Fahrenheit 451, and The Kite Runner. The ACLU sued on behalf of children on military bases in April 2025. On October 21, 2025, U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles ruled the removals reflected improper partisan motivation and ordered the books immediately restored.

title: One Big Beautiful Bill Strips Healthcare From 10 Million, Bans Planned Parenthood from Medicaid
synopsis: On July 4, 2025, Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21), which the Congressional Budget Office projected would cut over $990 billion from Medicaid and CHIP over a decade and leave 10 million more Americans uninsured by 2034. The law imposed Medicaid work requirements that threatened to eliminate coverage for 2.1 million women of reproductive age, and barred refugees and asylum seekers from Medicaid eligibility. Section 71113 prohibited Planned Parenthood — which serves over one million Medicaid patients — from receiving federal Medicaid payments for one year, prompting Planned Parenthood to announce the closure of at least 32 clinics across 11 states. The administration also withheld Title X family planning funds from 12 grantees affecting close to 300 clinics starting April 1, 2025. The Senate passed the bill 51-50 with Vice President JD Vance casting the tiebreaking vote.

title: Alien Enemies Act Mass Disappearances: Men Loaded on Planes With 24 Hours Notice and No Lawyer
synopsis: Beginning March 14-15, 2025, the Trump administration invoked the 1798 Alien Enemies Act via Proclamation 10903 to summarily remove Venezuelan nationals alleged to be Tren de Aragua members — bypassing all standard immigration court procedures. The government loaded detainees onto planes while a federal court hearing was underway, with one detainee described as having been on a plane for about forty minutes before being retrieved after a court order. In J.G.G. v. Trump, the Supreme Court confirmed 9-0 that AEA detainees are entitled to due process notice within a reasonable time. On May 16, 2025, in A.A.R.P. v. Trump, a 7-2 Supreme Court ruling found that providing only 24 hours notice devoid of information about how to exercise due process rights surely does not pass muster. One deportee had no gang affiliation — he told the court his tattoos came from a Google image search because he thought it looked cool.

title: Medicaid Cuts Target Disabled Americans: $900B Slashed, States Begin Re-Institutionalizing
synopsis: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4, 2025 cut a projected $900 billion-plus from Medicaid over a decade, and the June 2026 DOJ Olmstead opinion signaled the end of federal enforcement of community integration for people with disabilities. Iowa and other states began quietly reducing home health aide coverage and in-home support services that allow disabled people to avoid institutionalization. The Trump administration moved oversight of special education from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services under RFK Jr., whose public statements dismissing the severity of conditions like autism drew sharp rebukes from disability advocates. New Medicaid work requirements taking effect January 1, 2027 are expected to strip coverage from people with disabilities who cannot navigate complex exemption bureaucracies. Sen. Tammy Duckworth called the combination of cuts and DOJ opinion an attack on one of the most basic civil rights of Americans with disabilities.

title: ANWR Opened for Drilling on Inauguration Day
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14153, Unleashing Alaska's Extraordinary Resource Potential, immediately reversing Biden's halt on oil and gas drilling in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge's Coastal Plain. The order reinstated the 2020 leasing program, directed the Interior Department to rescind lease cancellations and issue new permits, and denied a pending Indigenous sacred site designation in the Coastal Plain. The area, covering roughly 1.5 million acres, is sacred to the Gwich'in people who call it the Sacred Place Where Life Begins. Environmental groups warned the move would devastate calving grounds of the Porcupine caribou herd and accelerate Arctic warming.

title: EPA Slashes 23% of Workforce, Shuts Down Science Office
synopsis: On July 18, 2025, the EPA announced it was cutting at least 3,700 employees — 23% of its 16,155-person workforce — and permanently closing its Office of Research and Development, which employed roughly 1,500 scientists. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin framed the $748.8 million in projected savings as organizational improvements, but critics noted the agency's enforcement, Superfund, and water offices were all targeted. Earlier, in February 2025, the agency had placed 168 environmental justice staff on administrative leave. The restructuring effectively returned EPA staffing to 1980s Reagan-era levels, gutting the scientific independence underpinning pollution regulation.

title: Bears Ears and Grand Staircase Shrunk 90% to Open Mining
synopsis: On July 13, 2026, Trump signed proclamations reducing Bears Ears National Monument by 91% — from 1.36 million acres to 121,096 acres — and Grand Staircase-Escalante by roughly 90%, leaving just 182,000 of its original 1.87 million acres protected. The cuts, even deeper than Trump's 2017 reductions which Biden had restored, opened nearly 3 million acres to uranium mining, coal extraction, and oil drilling. Utah Mining Association president Brian Somers confirmed the Bear Ears region sits in Utah's uranium belt and Grand Staircase contains our largest coal reserves. Five tribes challenged the move, and legal groups argued the Antiquities Act is a one-way statute that prohibits presidential reduction of monuments.

title: Clean Water Act Gutted: Millions of Wetland Acres Stripped of Protection
synopsis: On November 17, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced a proposed rule dramatically narrowing the definition of Waters of the United States (WOTUS) under the Clean Water Act, removing federal protections from vast swaths of wetlands and seasonal waterways. The rule implemented the Supreme Court's 2023 Sackett v. EPA decision in the most expansive way possible, excluding intermittent streams, isolated wetlands, and groundwater from federal jurisdiction. Zeldin accused prior Democratic administrations of having weaponized water definitions against farmers and developers. Environmental groups warned the rollback would leave hundreds of millions of acres of wetlands — critical for flood control, clean water filtration, and wildlife — vulnerable to pollution and destruction.

title: Federal Climate Science Purged: National Climate Assessments Taken Offline
synopsis: In June and July 2025, the Trump administration systematically erased decades of federally mandated climate science. NOAA shut down climate.gov on June 24, 2025, pursuant to Trump's May 23 executive order Restoring Gold Standard Science. The U.S. Global Change Research Program website — hosting all five National Climate Assessments — went dark on July 1, 2025. NASA initially promised to host the reports but reversed course on July 14, stating it had no legal obligation to do so. All 400 experts working on the congressionally mandated Sixth National Climate Assessment had been dismissed in April 2025, along with $4 million in Princeton ocean modeling funding. Former NOAA scientist Haley Crim wrote: Federal climate science is being systematically erased.

title: Methane Fee Killed, Industry Given 18-Month Pollution Pass
synopsis: On March 14, 2025, Trump signed Public Law 119-2 revoking the EPA's methane waste emissions charge rule under the Congressional Review Act, eliminating a fee of $900-$1,500 per ton on excess methane releases from oil and gas operations. Congress passed the repeal along party lines on February 26-27, 2025. Then on July 31, 2025, EPA issued an interim final rule bypassing public comment to extend methane compliance deadlines by 18 months, which the agency's own fact sheet acknowledged would result in 3.8 million additional tons of methane emissions between 2028 and 2038 — equivalent to the emissions from 25 million gasoline-powered vehicles driven for a year — plus 960,000 tons of volatile organic compounds and 36,000 tons of toxic air pollutants.

title: Superfund Budget Slashed 47%, Toxic Site Cleanups Halted
synopsis: Trump's FY2026 budget request, released May 2, 2025, proposed cutting the EPA's Hazardous Substance Superfund account by $254.9 million — a 47.4% reduction from the FY2025 enacted level of $537.7 million. The Superfund Remedial program, historically the largest component, was zeroed out from discretionary appropriations entirely, with the administration betting that Superfund tax receipts — which had already fallen 26% short of projections — would cover cleanups at the National Priorities List's most toxic sites. State and Tribal Assistance Grants were cut by $3.6 billion, an 83% reduction. The overall EPA budget request of $4.2 billion represented a 54.5% cut from FY2025 enacted levels.

title: Wildfire Season Sabotaged: Forest Service Loses 5,000 Staff
synopsis: As the U.S. entered an above-normal fire year in 2025, the Trump administration's workforce cuts and funding freezes crippled federal wildfire response. Approximately 5,000 Forest Service employees — about 15% of the agency — departed in the first five months of the administration, leaving fire crews to fill support roles instead of fighting fires. Trump froze billions in congressionally appropriated wildfire mitigation funding tied to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act, halting over 30 active fuel-reduction contracts held by groups like Oregon's Lomakatsi Restoration Project. A February 14, 2025 ProPublica investigation found seasonal hiring frozen, training programs canceled, and prescribed burn crews turned back mid-mission. Firefighter captain Ben McLane described a massive sledgehammer hitting the force during prime training season.

title: EPA Proposes Repealing All Greenhouse Gas Rules for Power Plants, Weakening Mercury Limits
synopsis: On June 11, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced proposals to repeal all greenhouse gas emissions standards for fossil fuel-fired power plants under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act and to weaken the 2024 Mercury and Air Toxics Standards that had been driving coal plant retirements. Zeldin called climate change action a cult and said the rollback would save the power sector $19 billion over two decades. The proposal included a novel legal argument that EPA must first determine whether power plant greenhouse gas emissions contribute significantly to dangerous air pollution before regulating — effectively pre-determining that they do not. Environmental groups warned the rules would expose millions to mercury, arsenic, and lead while accelerating planetary warming.

title: National Petroleum Reserve Alaska Opened: 82% of 23 Million Acres Unlocked
synopsis: On November 13, 2025, the Trump administration finalized a rollback of Biden-era limits on oil and gas drilling in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska, the largest tract of undisturbed public land in the United States. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum rescinded a 2024 rule that had prohibited leasing on 10.6 million acres and restricted development on 2 million more, reopening 82% of the 23-million-acre reserve. The Bureau of Land Management immediately initiated a lease sale process for winter 2025 — the first since 2019 — mandated under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4, 2025, which requires at least five lease sales by 2035 with each offering a minimum of 4 million acres. The reserve provides critical habitat for migratory birds, polar bears, and subsistence hunting communities.

title: FEMA Dismantled, Billion-Dollar Disaster Resilience Program Cancelled
synopsis: On April 3, 2025, an internal FEMA memo revealed the Trump administration's plan to cancel the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) program — the federal government's largest-ever climate adaptation initiative — clawing back over $750 million in congressionally appropriated grants. Twenty states sued FEMA, arguing the cancellation violated federal law. On June 11, 2025, Trump announced plans to phase out FEMA entirely, saying We want to wean off of FEMA. FEMA staffing fell 9.5% between January and June 2025. The administration denied at least 12 state disaster aid requests along largely partisan lines, including California wildfire recovery funds, while approving aid for Republican-governed states.

title: Offshore Drilling Proposed Off California and Florida for First Time in Decades
synopsis: On November 20, 2025, the Interior Department unveiled an expansive 11th National Outer Continental Shelf Oil and Gas Leasing Program for 2026-2031, proposing up to 34 lease sales across 21 of 27 OCS planning areas covering approximately 1.27 billion acres. Critically, it included six lease sales off the California coast — where no federal leasing had occurred since 1984 — and new areas in the Gulf of America, Arctic, and Florida's Gulf coast. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said the plan replaced the smallest offshore leasing plan ever published. The proposal drew bipartisan opposition from coastal states, including from Florida Republicans Gov. Ron DeSantis and Sen. Rick Scott, who said Florida's coasts must remain off the table.

title: Endangerment Finding Targeted: EPA Moves to Erase Legal Basis for All Climate Rules
synopsis: On July 29, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced a proposed rule to rescind the agency's 2009 endangerment finding — the scientific and legal declaration that greenhouse gases endanger public health and welfare, and the foundation for all U.S. climate regulation under the Clean Air Act. Zeldin called it the largest deregulatory action in the history of America, claiming it would save $52-54 billion annually in compliance costs. If finalized, the repeal would end greenhouse gas limits on vehicle tailpipes, power plants, and industrial sources, and cripple future administrations' ability to regulate CO2 without new congressional legislation. Legal experts noted the 2009 finding had survived numerous court challenges and was grounded in overwhelming scientific consensus.

title: Environmental Justice Program Wiped Out, 168 Staff Placed on Leave
synopsis: On February 6, 2025, the Trump administration placed approximately 168 EPA environmental justice staff on administrative leave and simultaneously pursued reductions at the Justice Department's environmental justice programs. The moves were part of Trump's broad executive orders abolishing diversity, equity, and inclusion programs across the federal government. EPA's FY2026 congressional budget justification, released in June 2025, allocated zero dollars and zero personnel to environmental justice community grants, technical assistance, and Superfund coordination for underserved communities. Environmental groups warned the rollback disproportionately endangered low-income and minority communities living near industrial polluters and Superfund sites.

title: U.S. Lobbies Nations to Kill Global Plastic Pollution Treaty
synopsis: In late July and early August 2025, the Trump administration actively lobbied foreign governments to reject binding caps on plastic production in the final round of UN global plastics treaty negotiations in Geneva. A memo dated July 25, 2025 circulated to countries at the start of talks outlined U.S. red lines explicitly opposing production limits and restrictions on chemical additives, placing Washington in direct opposition to over 100 countries. The U.S. position insisted on a narrow treaty focused solely on waste disposal, not upstream production controls. Without intervention, the OECD projects global plastic production will triple by 2060, choking oceans and accelerating climate change. Small island nations and the EU accused the Trump administration of single-handedly collapsing humanity's best chance at a binding plastics accord.

title: Capitol Breach Begins
synopsis: At approximately 2:12 PM on January 6, 2021, a violent mob of Trump supporters breached the US Capitol building, shattering windows and overwhelming Capitol Police. The rioters sought to halt the certification of the 2020 election results, marking the first time the Capitol was breached since 1814.

title: 140+ Police Officers Injured at Capitol
synopsis: During the January 6, 2021 insurrection, over 140 police officers from the Capitol Police and DC Metropolitan Police Departments sustained injuries. Officers suffered from traumatic brain injuries, cracked ribs, smashed spinal discs, and exposure to chemical irritants deployed by the mob.
